docs.title: SmartManipulator-X Operator PC — motion planning for a ROS 2 robot arm
docs.text: Quick start

docs.title: Plan a motion in three steps
docs.text:
No board and no arm are needed: the Robot PC runs ros2_control with mock hardware in Docker, and the Operator PC joins it on the same Docker network. Clone both repositories side by side — the Operator PC image takes the robot model from the Robot PC repository.

git clone https://github.com/SystemFromScratch/sfs-smartmanipulator-x-robot.git SmartManipulator-X-Robot-PC
git clone https://github.com/SystemFromScratch/sfs-smartmanipulator-x-operator.git SmartManipulator-X-Operator-PC

# terminal 1: the Robot PC (creates the network smx_net)
cd SmartManipulator-X-Robot-PC
docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up --build robot_pc

# terminal 2: the Operator PC (move_group + RViz2)
cd SmartManipulator-X-Operator-PC
docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up --build operator_pc

RViz2 opens with the MotionPlanning panel. Drag the interactive marker at the gripper, click Plan & Execute, and the Robot PC log shows arm_controller accepting the goal; the arm in RViz2 follows the /joint_states that come back over DDS (Planning in RViz2).

docs.title: Author
docs.text:
Anton Vynohradov · ORCID 0009-0005-6965-0911

Embedded Systems Engineer · Secure Product Architect · Founder of SystemFromScratch®

Embedded systems built from scratch — from bare metal to Linux, from first schematic to certification.

Anton designs and builds reliable, secure embedded products end to end: firmware, board support packages and drivers, RTOS and Embedded Linux platforms, hardware bring-up, and the security and compliance work needed to ship them. He is based in Poland and works remotely worldwide.

Area Focus Embedded software Bare-metal, RTOS and Linux firmware in C/C++, built to be maintained for years BSP & drivers Bootloaders, Zephyr drivers and Linux kernel work for MCUs, SoCs and SoC FPGAs Security & compliance Secure boot, threat modelling, MISRA C/C++, EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) readiness Industries Industrial IoT, automotive, robotics, medical and consumer electronics

Technology: C · C++ · Python · Zephyr RTOS · FreeRTOS · Embedded Linux · Yocto · Buildroot · ARM Cortex-M · STM32 · Microchip FPGA · RISC-V · CAN / ISO-TP · ROS 2 · Docker · Git · CI/CD · MISRA C/C++ · EU CRA

For SmartManipulator-X, Anton designed the system architecture, the Robot PC and Operator PC images and their ROS 2 configuration, the MoveIt 2 configuration of the Moveo, the robot description generated from the BCN3D Moveo CAD, the SmartFusion2 controller firmware with its motor tester, and this documentation.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: The Operator PC is one of the two ROS 2 computers of SmartManipulator-X. This page shows how its nodes connect to the Robot PC, what crosses the network, and which rules keep the two sides consistent. The architecture of the whole system (controller firmware, FPGA, hardware) is on the system site.

docs.title: ROS 2 graph
docs.text: ROS 2 graph: rviz2 and move_group on the Operator PC, robot_state_publisher, joint_state_broadcaster and ros2_control_node on the Robot PC, connected over ROS 2 DDS Node Computer Started by Role move_group Operator PC operator.launch.py Planning (OMPL), IK (pick_ik), planning scene, trajectory execution rviz2 Operator PC operator.launch.py (rviz:=true) MotionPlanning plugin, operator interface robot_state_publisher Robot PC robot.launch.py /robot_description, /tf from /joint_states ros2_control_node Robot PC robot.launch.py Controller manager at 100 Hz, hardware interface (mock now) joint_state_broadcaster Robot PC spawner /joint_states from the hardware state interfaces arm_controller, gripper_controller Robot PC spawner joint_trajectory_controller, position command interface

docs.title: What crosses the network
docs.text:
Interface Type Direction Used for /joint_states topic sensor_msgs/JointState Robot PC → Operator PC Current state of the arm for move_group and RViz2 /tf, /tf_static topics Robot PC → Operator PC Frames of the robot (RViz2 TF and RobotModel displays) /robot_description topic, transient local both Published by robot_state_publisher and, with the same model, by move_group (publish_robot_description); read by the RobotModel display (off by default) /arm_controller/follow_joint_trajectory action control_msgs/FollowJointTrajectory Operator PC → Robot PC Arm trajectories (J1–J5) /gripper_controller/follow_joint_trajectory action control_msgs/FollowJointTrajectory Operator PC → Robot PC Gripper trajectories /display_planned_path, /monitored_planning_scene, MoveIt actions and services inside the Operator PC RViz2 ↔ move_group

Nothing else is needed from the Robot PC: no controller-manager services, no USB device, no file system.

docs.title: The robot model on both sides
docs.text:
move_group and RViz2 do not read /robot_description from the Robot PC to plan. The launch file expands the same Xacro file the Robot PC uses — smartmanipulator_x_description/urdf/smartmanipulator_x.urdf.xacro — which the image build copied from the Robot PC repository (see build contexts):

MoveItConfigsBuilder("smartmanipulator_x", package_name="smartmanipulator_x_moveit_config")
    # Same model as the Robot PC; the hardware block is irrelevant to MoveIt.
    .robot_description(file_path=description_xacro, mappings={"use_mock_hardware": "true"})

The use_mock_hardware mapping only selects the ros2_control block of the Xacro, which MoveIt ignores. Links, joints, limits and meshes are identical to the Robot PC's — as long as both images were built from the same Robot PC commit. After a change to the robot description, rebuild both images.

docs.title: Responsibilities and boundaries
docs.text: Rule Why The Operator PC never opens the controller's USB device; do not pass /dev/ttyACM0 to it Only the Robot PC owns the hardware path and its safety No URDF/Xacro in this repository; consume smartmanipulator_x_description One canonical model, generated from the Moveo CAD No OpenMANIPULATOR-X model or configuration as a stand-in for the Moveo Different geometry, joints and actuators Controller names and joints in moveit_controllers.yaml match controllers.yaml of the Robot PC Otherwise MoveIt cannot find the action servers or the joints do not match MoveIt 2, RViz2 and (later) Gazebo stay out of the Robot PC image The Robot PC stays lean and headless ROS 2 data goes over DDS, never over SSH SSH is for administration only

docs.title: Real robot and simulation
docs.text:
The same MoveIt configuration is meant to drive either path; the robot model, joint names, limits, planning groups and controller semantics must agree in both:

One MoveIt configuration, three control paths: the real robot through the Robot PC and the DYNAMIXEL path (after hardware verification), mock hardware on the Robot PC (in use today), and Gazebo simulation (planned)

Today the Operator PC drives the mock path. The real path becomes available when the Robot PC enables its verified DYNAMIXEL hardware configuration; nothing changes on the Operator PC for that. Gazebo integration will live in this repository.

docs.title: Package layout
docs.text:
ros2_ws/src/smartmanipulator_x_moveit_config/
├── package.xml                     ament_cmake; exec-depends on MoveIt, pick_ik, RViz2, the description
├── CMakeLists.txt                  installs config/, launch/, rviz/
├── config/
│   ├── smartmanipulator_x.srdf     planning groups, named states, end effector, collision matrix
│   ├── kinematics.yaml             pick_ik, position-only
│   ├── joint_limits.yaml           accelerations and default scaling
│   └── moveit_controllers.yaml     arm_controller, gripper_controller, execution tolerances
├── launch/operator.launch.py       move_group + RViz2
└── rviz/moveit.rviz                RViz2 layout

Each file is described in MoveIt 2 configuration.

docs.title: Development
docs.text: This page describes how the Operator PC repository is organized and built: the Docker image, the ROS 2 package, the VS Code tasks, the documentation and CI. The Robot PC has its own development page.

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text:
.
├── docker/
│   ├── Dockerfile                    Operator PC image (ros:jazzy-ros-base + MoveIt 2 + RViz2 + workspace)
│   ├── docker-compose.yml            operator_pc and shell services on smx_net
│   ├── entrypoint.sh                 sources ROS 2 and the built workspace
│   └── env.example                   template for docker/.env
├── ros2_ws/src/
│   └── smartmanipulator_x_moveit_config/   SRDF, kinematics, limits, controllers, launch, RViz2
├── tools/docs/                       PDF manual builder, figures, MkDocs hook
├── docs/, overrides/, mkdocs.yml     this documentation
├── requirements-docs.txt             documentation tools (.venv)
└── .vscode/tasks.json                Operator PC and documentation tasks

Generated directories (ros2_ws/build/, ros2_ws/install/, ros2_ws/log/, site/, build/, docs/downloads/, .venv/) are ignored by Git, and the documentation is kept out of the Docker build context by .dockerignore.

docs.title: Working on the MoveIt configuration
docs.text:
The workspace is built into the image, not bind-mounted. After a change under ros2_ws/src/:

docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up --build operator_pc

Rules that keep the two computers consistent:

  • Do not add a URDF/Xacro here. Change the robot description in the Robot PC repository and rebuild both images.
  • Joint names, planning groups, controller names and the joints of each controller must match smartmanipulator_x_description and the Robot PC's controllers.yaml.
  • Keep Operator-only dependencies (MoveIt, RViz2, Gazebo, GUI libraries) in this image; never add them to the Robot PC image.
  • The Operator PC gets no USB device and no ros2_control hardware interface.

For a quick test of a configuration file without a rebuild, mount it over the installed copy, for example:

docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml run --rm \
    -v "$PWD/ros2_ws/src/smartmanipulator_x_moveit_config/config:/ws/install/smartmanipulator_x_moveit_config/share/smartmanipulator_x_moveit_config/config" \
    operator_pc

Stop operator_pc first (fixed address); rebuild before you commit.

docs.title: VS Code tasks
docs.text:
.vscode/tasks.json runs Docker Compose from the repository root. Ctrl+Shift+B opens a picker with every task of the build group; none is the default, so the picker always appears.

Task Group Command Operator PC: Start (move_group + RViz2) build docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up --build operator_pc Operator PC: Stop build docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml down Operator PC: Rebuild and restart build Stop, then up --build --force-recreate operator_pc Operator PC: Build image build build operator_pc Operator PC: Rebuild image (no cache) build build --no-cache --pull operator_pc Docs: Build PDF manual build python tools/docs/build_manual.py in .venv Operator PC: Shell – run --rm shell Docs: Live preview – mkdocs serve in .venv

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The documentation is the Markdown in docs/. MkDocs Material turns it into the website, and tools/docs/build_manual.py turns the same pages into the printable A4 user manual (cover, imprint, contents with page numbers, numbered chapters, running headers, PDF bookmarks), rendered with WeasyPrint. Both follow the SystemFromScratch® documentation style of the Robot PC documentation; the landing page is configured in mkdocs.yml → extra.landing and the manual in mkdocs.yml → extra.manual.

Set up the tools once in the repository .venv. WeasyPrint needs the Pango library: on Windows from MSYS2 (pacman -S mingw-w64-x86_64-pango; the builder finds C:\msys64\mingw64\bin by itself), on Ubuntu apt install libpango-1.0-0 libpangoft2-1.0-0.

# Windows (PowerShell, repository root)
py -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements-docs.txt

# Linux (repository root)
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
Command Result python -m mkdocs serve Live preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000 python -m mkdocs build Static website in site/ (strict: a broken link fails the build) python tools/docs/build_manual.py build/manual/SmartManipulator-X_Operator_PC_User_Manual_v<version>.pdf; the version is the latest vX.Y.Z tag python tools/docs/build_manual.py --output docs/downloads/SmartManipulator-X_Operator_PC_User_Manual.pdf The file the website links to (CI does this before deploying) python tools/docs/diagrams.py Regenerates the hero docs/assets/images/hero-3d.svg and the diagrams system-overview.svg, ros-graph.svg, control-paths.svg, smx-net.svg, image-build.svg python tools/docs/diagrams.py --no-hero Only the diagrams (no Robot PC checkout needed)

The hero draws the real arm: tools/docs/hero_robot.py reads the URDF/Xacro and the visual meshes of smartmanipulator_x_description from the Robot PC repository (SMX_ROBOT_PC_REPO, default ../SmartManipulator-X-Robot-PC) and places them by forward kinematics; the glowing tool path above the arm is the fingertip position computed the same way. Run it again after the description changes.

Writing rules that keep the website and the PDF correct:

  • Start every page with exactly one # Title; chapter and section numbers are added in the PDF, so do not number headings by hand.
  • Add a new page to nav in mkdocs.yml, otherwise it is missing from the site and the PDF.
  • An image on a line of its own, ![Caption](assets/images/file.svg), becomes a figure with its alt text as the caption (tools/docs/hooks.py).
  • Link to other pages with relative .md paths; strict mode checks them, and the PDF turns them into page references.
  • Diagrams are SVG files generated by tools/docs/diagrams.py; the PDF renderer runs no JavaScript.
  • Every value in the documentation (addresses, limits, parameters) comes from the files of this repository or the Robot PC repository; change the page together with the file.

docs.title: CI
docs.text:
Workflow Trigger Does documentation.yml Push to main; manual Builds the PDF manual into docs/downloads/, then mkdocs gh-deploy publishes the website with the PDF to GitHub Pages (branch gh-pages)

Enable GitHub Pages for the gh-pages branch in the repository settings once; the site is then at https://systemfromscratch.github.io/sfs-smartmanipulator-x-operator/.

docs.title: Docker image and Compose
docs.text:
The Operator PC runs entirely in Docker: one image, two Compose services, and the GUI shown on the host through WSLg (Windows 11) or X11 (Linux). ROS 2 is not installed on the host.

File Content docker/Dockerfile ros:jazzy-ros-base with MoveIt 2, pick_ik, RViz2; builds the workspace docker/docker-compose.yml operator_pc (move_group + RViz2) and shell (profile tools) on the network smx_net docker/entrypoint.sh Sources ROS 2 and the built workspace, then runs the command docker/env.example Template for docker/.env .dockerignore Keeps build output, editor files and the documentation out of the build context (the repository root)

docs.title: The image
docs.text:
Build contexts of the image: the Operator PC repository and the Robot PC repository feed the ros:jazzy-ros-base build, which produces the smartmanipulator-x-operator:jazzy image with the Fast DDS profile Step Content Base ros:jazzy-ros-base (Ubuntu 24.04, ROS 2 Jazzy) Packages ros-jazzy-moveit, ros-jazzy-pick-ik, ros-jazzy-rviz2, ros-jazzy-xacro, ros-jazzy-urdf, ros-jazzy-ros2controlcli, ros-jazzy-control-msgs, python3-colcon-common-extensions, Mesa (libgl1-mesa-dri, mesa-utils) Robot description smartmanipulator_x_description from the Robot PC repository → /ws/src/smartmanipulator_x_description DDS profile docker/dds/fastdds_udp.xml from the Robot PC repository → /etc/smx/fastdds_udp.xml Project packages ros2_ws/src of this repository → /ws/src/operator Build colcon build --symlink-install, RelWithDebInfo Shell .bashrc sources /opt/ros/jazzy and /ws/install, so docker exec … bash has ROS 2 ready

Environment of the image:

Variable Value ROS_DISTRO jazzy ROS_WS /ws RMW_IMPLEMENTATION rmw_fastrtps_cpp ROS_DOMAIN_ID 42 (Compose overrides it from docker/.env) FASTDDS_DEFAULT_PROFILES_FILE, FASTRTPS_DEFAULT_PROFILES_FILE /etc/smx/fastdds_udp.xml TZ Europe/Warsaw

The image tag is smartmanipulator-x-operator:jazzy (SMX_OPERATOR_IMAGE).

docs.title: Build contexts
docs.text:
The robot description and the DDS profile are not copied into this repository. The Dockerfile reads them from a second build context, robot_pc_repo, which Compose points at the Robot PC checkout:

build:
  context: ..
  dockerfile: docker/Dockerfile
  additional_contexts:
    # Canonical robot description and DDS profile.
    robot_pc_repo: ${SMX_ROBOT_PC_REPO:-../../SmartManipulator-X-Robot-PC}

COPY --from=robot_pc_repo ros2_ws/src/smartmanipulator_x/smartmanipulator_x_description \
     ${ROS_WS}/src/smartmanipulator_x_description
COPY --from=robot_pc_repo docker/dds/fastdds_udp.xml /etc/smx/fastdds_udp.xml

So both computers always use the same joints and transport settings. The relative path is resolved from docker/; the default expects both repositories side by side. This needs Docker Compose v2.17 or later and BuildKit.

To build without Compose:

docker build -f docker/Dockerfile \
    --build-context robot_pc_repo=../SmartManipulator-X-Robot-PC \
    -t smartmanipulator-x-operator:jazzy .

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
Service Profile Network Command Use operator_pc default smx_net, fixed 10.77.0.20 (SMX_OPERATOR_IP) ros2 launch smartmanipulator_x_moveit_config operator.launch.py move_group + RViz2 shell tools smx_net, dynamic address bash (interactive) ROS 2 CLI, rviz2 alone, glxgears

Both use init: true (a small init process reaps child processes) and the same ROS and GUI environment. operator_pc stops with SIGINT, like Ctrl+C in a terminal, so ros2 launch shuts its nodes down cleanly.

docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up --build operator_pc     # start
docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml run --rm shell             # shell
docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml build operator_pc          # rebuild only
docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml build --no-cache --pull operator_pc   # from scratch
docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml down                       # remove containers

smx_net is declared external: it belongs to the Robot PC Compose project, which creates it. down here leaves it in place.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
Every value has a default in docker-compose.yml. Copy docker/env.example to docker/.env only to change one; docker/.env is ignored by Git.

Variable Default Meaning ROS_DOMAIN_ID 42 Must match the Robot PC SMX_OPERATOR_IP 10.77.0.20 Address of operator_pc on smx_net (the Robot PC is 10.77.0.10) SMX_ROBOT_PC_REPO ../../SmartManipulator-X-Robot-PC Robot PC checkout, relative to docker/ or absolute SMX_OPERATOR_IMAGE smartmanipulator-x-operator:jazzy Image name and tag SMX_X11_DIR /run/desktop/mnt/host/wslg/.X11-unix Host directory mounted as /tmp/.X11-unix SMX_WSLG_DIR /run/desktop/mnt/host/wslg Host directory mounted as /mnt/wslg SMX_DISPLAY :0 DISPLAY SMX_WAYLAND_DISPLAY wayland-0 WAYLAND_DISPLAY SMX_XDG_RUNTIME_DIR /mnt/wslg/runtime-dir XDG_RUNTIME_DIR SMX_PULSE_SERVER /mnt/wslg/PulseServer PULSE_SERVER (WSLg audio; unused by RViz2) SMX_LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE 1 1: software OpenGL (llvmpipe)

Fixed in the Compose file: RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_fastrtps_cpp, ROS_AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY_RANGE=SUBNET, QT_QPA_PLATFORM=xcb, QT_X11_NO_MITSHM=1.

docs.title: GUI on Windows 11 (WSLg)
docs.text: The defaults are made for Docker Desktop with the WSL 2 backend. Docker Desktop exposes the WSLg sockets of its VM under /run/desktop/mnt/host/wslg; Compose mounts them into the container, and RViz2 draws through X11 (QT_QPA_PLATFORM=xcb) on the WSLg display :0. Nothing has to be configured; run the Compose commands from PowerShell or from a WSL distribution.

docs.title: GUI on a Linux desktop (X11)
docs.text:
Allow local containers to connect to your X server once per session, and set the X11 values in docker/.env:

xhost +local:docker
cp docker/env.example docker/.env

# docker/.env
SMX_X11_DIR=/tmp/.X11-unix
SMX_WSLG_DIR=/tmp/smx-no-wslg
SMX_DISPLAY=:0
SMX_XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/tmp

SMX_DISPLAY must match echo $DISPLAY on the host. SMX_WSLG_DIR only needs to be a path that exists or can be created; nothing is used from it on Linux.

docs.title: Rendering
docs.text: LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 (Mesa llvmpipe) is the default because it works on every host, without GPU drivers in the container. RViz2 with the Moveo model is usable this way; it costs CPU. With a working GPU path (for example /dev/dri passed through on Linux with a Compose override, or the WSLg D3D12 driver), set SMX_LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=0. Check with glxinfo -B or glxgears in the shell service which renderer is in use.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: This guide takes you from two fresh clones to RViz2 planning motions for the SmartManipulator-X arm. Everything runs in Docker on one computer: the Robot PC with mock hardware (every commanded joint position becomes the joint state at once) and the Operator PC on the same Docker network. No controller board and no arm are needed.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Where What Windows 11 Docker Desktop with the WSL 2 backend. RViz2 is shown through WSLg, which Docker Desktop shares with its containers Linux desktop Docker Engine and an X11 session (Wayland desktops with XWayland work too) Both Git, Docker Compose v2.17 or later (for additional_contexts) and BuildKit (the default) Optional VS Code

ROS 2 is not installed on the host: it comes with the images (ros:jazzy-ros-base). Check the Compose version with docker compose version.

docs.title: Clone both repositories side by side
docs.text:
The Operator PC image takes the robot description and the Fast DDS profile from the Robot PC repository. By default it looks for it next to this repository, under the name SmartManipulator-X-Robot-PC:

git clone https://github.com/SystemFromScratch/sfs-smartmanipulator-x-robot.git SmartManipulator-X-Robot-PC
git clone https://github.com/SystemFromScratch/sfs-smartmanipulator-x-operator.git SmartManipulator-X-Operator-PC

SmartManipulator-X/
├── SmartManipulator-X-Robot-PC/       Robot PC: ros2_control, robot description, DDS profile
└── SmartManipulator-X-Operator-PC/    Operator PC: this repository

If the Robot PC checkout lives elsewhere, set SMX_ROBOT_PC_REPO in docker/.env (see Docker image and Compose).

docs.title: 1. Start the Robot PC
docs.text:
In the Robot PC repository:

docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up --build robot_pc

The first run builds the image, which takes several minutes. Compose creates the Docker network smx_net (10.77.0.0/24), which stands in for the Ethernet link between the two computers, and starts the Robot PC at 10.77.0.10 with robot_state_publisher, ros2_control_node (mock hardware), joint_state_broadcaster, arm_controller and gripper_controller. Leave the terminal open.

Start the Robot PC first

The Operator PC declares smx_net as an external network. If the Robot PC has not created it yet, Compose stops with network smx_net declared as external, but could not be found.

docs.title: 2. Start the Operator PC
docs.text:
In this repository, in a second terminal:

docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up --build operator_pc

The first build installs MoveIt 2, pick_ik and RViz2 on top of ros:jazzy-ros-base and builds the workspace (several minutes). The container joins smx_net at 10.77.0.20 and runs:

ros2 launch smartmanipulator_x_moveit_config operator.launch.py

which starts move_group and RViz2. The log of move_group ends with You can start planning now! once it has received the robot state from the Robot PC.

docs.title: 3. Plan and execute
docs.text:
RViz2 opens with the MotionPlanning display, planning group arm: the current state of the arm (as reported by the Robot PC) is opaque, the goal state is orange and semi-transparent.

  1. Drag the interactive marker at the gripper (tool_link) to a new position.
  2. In the Planning tab, click Plan & Execute.
  3. The Robot PC log shows arm_controller accepting and finishing the goal. The arm in RViz2 follows the /joint_states that come back from the Robot PC.

For the named poses, the gripper and the planning options, see Planning in RViz2.

docs.title: Shell on the same network
docs.text:
The shell service (profile tools) is a second container with the same image, network and GUI setup, for the ROS 2 command line:

docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml run --rm shell

ros2 node list                    # /move_group, /rviz2 and the Robot PC nodes
ros2 control list_controllers     # arm_controller, gripper_controller, joint_state_broadcaster
ros2 topic echo /joint_states --once
glxgears                          # checks the display path

docs.title: Stop and rebuild
docs.text:
Stop with Ctrl+C, or remove the Operator PC containers (the network belongs to the Robot PC project and stays):

docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml down

The workspace and the robot description are built into the image, not mounted. After changing the MoveIt configuration here, or the robot description in the Robot PC repository, start with up --build again.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Planning in RViz2: named poses, the gripper, planning options.
  • Architecture: which node runs where and what goes over DDS.
  • Network and DDS: two computers on a real network.

docs.title: MoveIt 2 configuration
docs.text:
smartmanipulator_x_moveit_config is the only ROS 2 package of the Operator PC. It holds the semantic description, the kinematics, the planning limits, the controller mapping, the launch file and the RViz2 layout. The robot description itself (URDF/Xacro, meshes) comes from the Robot PC repository.

The configuration is loaded with MoveItConfigsBuilder in launch/operator.launch.py:

Builder call File robot_description smartmanipulator_x_description/urdf/smartmanipulator_x.urdf.xacro (Robot PC) robot_description_semantic config/smartmanipulator_x.srdf robot_description_kinematics config/kinematics.yaml joint_limits config/joint_limits.yaml trajectory_execution config/moveit_controllers.yaml planning_pipelines ompl only, default ompl (MoveIt's default OMPL settings) planning_scene_monitor publishes the robot description, the semantic description, the planning scene, geometry, state and transform updates

docs.title: Semantic description (SRDF)
docs.text: config/smartmanipulator_x.srdf. Link and joint names come from smartmanipulator_x_description.

docs.title: Planning groups
docs.text:
Group Definition Joints arm chain base_link → tool_link j1_base, j2_shoulder, j3_elbow, j4_forearm_roll, j5_wrist gripper joint gripper gripper (the other gripper joints mimic it)

The end effector gripper is attached to link5, with arm as parent group.

docs.title: Named states
docs.text:
Group State j1_base j2_shoulder j3_elbow j4_forearm_roll j5_wrist arm home 0 0 0 0 0 arm ready 0 0.5 0.8 0 0.6 arm cad_pose 0 0.7416 0.4674 0.1426 0.9151 Group State gripper gripper open 0.0 gripper closed 1.4

Values in rad. cad_pose is the pose of the BCN3D CAD assembly from which the robot description was generated.

docs.title: Collision matrix
docs.text:
The SRDF disables collision checking only where contact is part of the design:

  • Adjacent links: base_link–link1, link1–link2, link2–link3, link3–link4, link4–link5, and link5 against every gripper part.
  • Gripper parts against each other (servo_gear, idler_gear, pivot_left, pivot_right, finger_left, finger_right): gears, pivot arms and fingers touch by design.

All other pairs are checked. The convex-hull collision meshes of the description overlap nowhere else at the zero, ready and CAD assembly poses (checked with tools/cad/collide.py in the Robot PC repository). Re-check after the description changes, and add a pair only with its reason.

docs.title: Kinematics
docs.text:
config/kinematics.yaml — pick_ik for the arm group:

Parameter Value Meaning kinematics_solver pick_ik/PickIkPlugin kinematics_solver_timeout 0.05 s Per IK call kinematics_solver_attempts 3 mode global Global search (finds solutions far from the seed) position_scale 1.0 The tool position counts fully rotation_scale 0.0 The tool orientation is ignored position_threshold 0.001 m A solution must be within 1 mm orientation_threshold 0.01 rad Not relevant with rotation_scale 0 cost_threshold 0.001 minimal_displacement_weight 0.0 No preference for small joint motions gd_step_size 0.0001 Gradient descent step

Why position-only: the Moveo has five arm joints, so it cannot reach an arbitrary 6-D pose. With a full pose goal, most marker positions in RViz2 would have no solution. With rotation_scale: 0.0 the marker always solves for the tool position. For a best-effort orientation, raise rotation_scale (for example to 0.5): pick_ik then trades position and orientation error, and the result may miss the position by more than 1 mm.

docs.title: Joint limits
docs.text:
The position and velocity limits come from the robot description (all arm joints and the gripper: 1.0 rad/s). config/joint_limits.yaml adds what the URDF cannot express:

Setting Value default_velocity_scaling_factor 0.3 default_acceleration_scaling_factor 0.3 max_velocity (every joint) 1.0 rad/s max_acceleration (every joint) 1.0 rad/s²

The default scaling factors apply to requests that do not set their own scaling, for example from scripts. The RViz2 MotionPlanning panel always sends its own Velocity Scaling and Accel. Scaling, which start at 0.10 (see Planning in RViz2).

Joint Position limits in the description (rad) j1_base −π … π j2_shoulder −π/2 … π/2 j3_elbow −π/2 … π/2 j4_forearm_roll −π … π j5_wrist −π/2 … π/2 gripper 0 … 1.45

Placeholders

All limits are placeholders until the Moveo axes are measured on the real arm. Update the position and velocity limits in the robot description (Robot PC repository) and the accelerations here, then rebuild both images.

docs.title: Controllers
docs.text:
config/moveit_controllers.yaml maps the planning groups to the action servers of the Robot PC. The names must match controllers.yaml of the Robot PC repository.

MoveIt controller Type Action Joints arm_controller FollowJointTrajectory arm_controller/follow_joint_trajectory j1_base … j5_wrist gripper_controller FollowJointTrajectory gripper_controller/follow_joint_trajectory gripper

Both are default: true. The controller manager is MoveItSimpleControllerManager: it only needs the action servers, no access to the Robot PC's controller manager.

Execution setting Value Effect allowed_execution_duration_scaling 1.5 Execution may take 1.5 × the planned duration… allowed_goal_duration_margin 1.0 s …plus 1 s, then MoveIt cancels it allowed_start_tolerance 0.02 rad The arm must start within this of the plan's first point

On the Robot PC side, arm_controller and gripper_controller are joint_trajectory_controller/JointTrajectoryController with a position command interface and position + velocity state interfaces, at 100 Hz.

docs.title: Launch file
docs.text:
launch/operator.launch.py starts two nodes:

Node Parameters Condition move_group (moveit_ros_move_group) the complete MoveIt configuration always rviz2 -d rviz/moveit.rviz; robot description, semantic description, kinematics, planning pipelines, joint limits rviz:=true (default) 
ros2 launch smartmanipulator_x_moveit_config operator.launch.py            # move_group + RViz2
ros2 launch smartmanipulator_x_moveit_config operator.launch.py rviz:=false  # move_group only

docs.title: Changing the configuration
docs.text:
1. Edit the files under ros2_ws/src/smartmanipulator_x_moveit_config/.
  2. Rebuild and restart: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up --build operator_pc (the package is built into the image).
  3. If joint names, groups or controllers change, change the Robot PC (controllers.yaml, the description) in the same step, and rebuild both images.

docs.title: Network and DDS
docs.text: The Operator PC and the Robot PC talk only through ROS 2 DDS, like two computers on an Ethernet. On one computer, the Docker network smx_net stands in for that cable; on two computers, the real network does. The domain ID and the DDS profile stay the same in both cases.

docs.title: One computer: smx_net
docs.text: The Docker network smx_net on one computer: robot_pc at 10.77.0.10, operator_pc at 10.77.0.20 and the shell container, all on ROS 2 DDS with Fast DDS over UDPv4 and ROS_DOMAIN_ID 42 Setting Robot PC Operator PC Network creates smx_net (10.77.0.0/24, SMX_SUBNET) joins it as external Address 10.77.0.10 (SMX_ROBOT_IP) 10.77.0.20 (SMX_OPERATOR_IP) ROS_DOMAIN_ID 42 42 RMW_IMPLEMENTATION rmw_fastrtps_cpp rmw_fastrtps_cpp Fast DDS profile docker/dds/fastdds_udp.xml the same file, copied at build time to /etc/smx/fastdds_udp.xml ROS_AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY_RANGE SUBNET

docs.title: The Fast DDS profile: UDP only
docs.text:
Fast DDS uses shared memory between participants it believes are on the same host. Containers on one computer have separate /dev/shm, so discovery can succeed while no data arrives — the nodes are listed, but topics stay silent. The profile disables the built-in transports and keeps all traffic on UDPv4:

<participant profile_name="smx_udp_only" is_default_profile="true">
  <rtps>
    <userTransports>
      <transport_id>smx_udpv4</transport_id>
    </userTransports>
    <useBuiltinTransports>false</useBuiltinTransports>
  </rtps>
</participant>

UDP is also what the real Ethernet link carries, so simulation and hardware use the same transport. The file belongs to the Robot PC repository; the image build copies it, so a change there reaches the Operator PC with the next --build.

docs.title: Two computers: real Ethernet
docs.text:
When the Robot PC moves to its own board (Raspberry Pi CM4, Jetson or an Ubuntu 24.04 PC), replace smx_net by the host network on both sides:

  1. In both Compose files, remove the networks entries of the services and the smx_net declaration, and add network_mode: host.
  2. Keep ROS_DOMAIN_ID, RMW_IMPLEMENTATION and the Fast DDS profile unchanged.
  3. Make sure both computers are in one subnet and the firewall lets DDS through (UDP, ports 7400 and up for domain 42 — the RTPS ports are computed from the domain ID; the simplest rule allows UDP between the two hosts).
  4. Check discovery from both sides with ros2 node list, then ros2 topic echo /joint_states --once on the Operator PC.

network_mode: host gives a container the network of the Docker host. On Linux that is the real network. With Docker Desktop on Windows the Docker host is a VM, so a host-mode container is not necessarily reachable from the Robot PC; verify discovery in both directions, or run the Operator PC on a Linux computer for two-host operation.

docs.title: Native Windows ROS 2 cannot join
docs.text: ROS 2 installed natively on Windows does not discover the containers on smx_net: Docker Desktop does not route multicast between Windows and its container networks. Run every ROS 2 node of the system in a container on that network — for the command line, use the shell service.

docs.title: SSH is not a ROS transport
docs.text: SSH is for administration (logs, updates, starting containers on the Robot PC). ROS 2 topics and actions always go over DDS; do not tunnel or forward them through SSH.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text: Check Command (in the shell service) Expected Same domain echo $ROS_DOMAIN_ID 42 on both sides Discovery ros2 node list /move_group, /rviz2, /robot_state_publisher, /controller_manager, … Joint states ros2 topic echo /joint_states --once Six joint names with positions Controllers ros2 control list_controllers arm_controller, gripper_controller, joint_state_broadcaster active Actions ros2 action list /arm_controller/follow_joint_trajectory, /gripper_controller/follow_joint_trajectory Profile echo $FASTDDS_DEFAULT_PROFILES_FILE /etc/smx/fastdds_udp.xml

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
SmartManipulator-X is a robot arm project. It combines the ROS 2 control and operator-software concepts of ROBOTIS OpenMANIPULATOR-X with the mechanical design of BCN3D Moveo. A Microchip SmartFusion2 controller drives the stepper motors of the Moveo joints and a hobby servo on the gripper, and presents them to the ROS 2 host as virtual DYNAMIXEL devices over Protocol 2.0.

This documentation covers the Operator PC: the computer on which the operator plans motions and watches the arm. The whole system — the Robot PC, the controller firmware, the hardware and the mechanics — is documented on the SmartManipulator-X system site, which is published from the Robot PC repository.

docs.title: What the Operator PC does
docs.text:
Owns Does not own MoveIt 2 motion planning (move_group, OMPL, pick_ik) The USB link to the SmartFusion2 controller (/dev/ttyACM0) RViz2 with the MotionPlanning panel ros2_control, the controllers and the hardware interface The semantic robot description (SRDF), kinematics, planning limits, controller mapping The robot description (URDF/Xacro and meshes) — it is consumed from the Robot PC repository Its Docker image, Compose services and GUI setup The motor drivers, the firmware, the power and the emergency stop Simulation workflows (Gazebo: planned, not in this repository yet)

The Operator PC never talks to the motor controllers. It plans in MoveIt and sends the trajectories as FollowJointTrajectory actions over ROS 2 DDS to the Robot PC, which runs ros2_control:

SmartManipulator-X with the Operator PC in focus: trajectories go over ROS 2 DDS to the Robot PC, which drives the controller and the arm

docs.title: System components
docs.text: Component Role Platform Operator PC (this repository) Motion planning and visualization: MoveIt 2, RViz2; simulation later ROS 2 Jazzy in Docker; DDS client of the Robot PC Robot PC Robot-side ROS 2 control: ros2_control, the ROBOTIS hardware interface and DynamixelSDK; owns the USB link to the controller Ubuntu 24.04, ROS 2 Jazzy in Docker Controller firmware DYNAMIXEL Protocol 2.0 device: six stepper axes (IDs 1–6), the gripper servo (ID 7) and a controller device (ID 200) Zephyr RTOS on the SmartFusion2 Cortex-M3 FPGA design Pin routing of SPI and UART, CorePWM for the gripper servo SmartFusion2 FPGA fabric Drives Six TMC5160 modules in motion-controller mode, MG996R gripper servo 24 V and 6 V supplies Mechanics Joints, links and printed parts BCN3D Moveo

docs.title: Repositories
docs.text:
Repository Content Documentation sfs-smartmanipulator-x-operator This repository: Operator PC image, MoveIt 2 configuration, RViz2 setup, this documentation This site; the system view in Operator PC sfs-smartmanipulator-x-robot Robot PC image and ROS 2 workspace, the robot description generated from the Moveo CAD, the Fast DDS profile, the system documentation Robot PC, BCN3D Moveo mechanics SmartManipulator-X-Controller Zephyr firmware of the SmartFusion2 and the motor tester GUI Firmware, Motor tester GUI SmartManipulator-X-Libero FPGA design of the SmartFusion2 Hardware

The two computer repositories are checked out side by side. The Operator PC image build reads the robot description and the DDS profile from the Robot PC checkout (default path ../SmartManipulator-X-Robot-PC), see Docker image and Compose.

docs.title: Joint contract
docs.text:
The Operator PC, the Robot PC and the real hardware use the same joint names. They are defined in smartmanipulator_x_description in the Robot PC repository; the Operator PC only refers to them.

Joint Moveo axis DYNAMIXEL ID (SmartFusion2) MoveIt group Controller j1_base J1 base 1 arm arm_controller j2_shoulder J2 shoulder 2 and 3 (two mirrored motors) arm arm_controller j3_elbow J3 elbow 4 arm arm_controller j4_forearm_roll J4 forearm roll 5 arm arm_controller j5_wrist J5 wrist 6 arm arm_controller gripper gripper servo 7 gripper gripper_controller

The gripper linkage has mimic joints (gripper_idler_gear, gripper_pivot_*, gripper_finger_*) that follow gripper; they are neither planned nor commanded.

docs.title: Current status
docs.text:
• Operator PC (this repository): ROS 2 Jazzy image with MoveIt 2, pick_ik and RViz2; move_group and RViz2 start with one Compose command, join smx_net, plan with OMPL and execute through the Robot PC's arm_controller and gripper_controller, with the Robot PC running mock hardware on the same computer.
  • Robot model: generated from the BCN3D Moveo CAD in the Robot PC repository. Joint limits are still placeholders until measured on the real arm; the MoveIt joint limits of this repository are conservative placeholders as well.
  • Real hardware: not reachable from the Operator PC yet — the Robot PC refuses use_mock_hardware:=false until its real-hardware ros2_control path is verified (see the Robot PC documentation).
  • Open items: Gazebo simulation on the Operator PC, measured joint limits and velocities, two-host operation over real Ethernet, orientation goals with a 5-DOF-aware IK setting.

docs.title: Planning in RViz2
docs.text:
RViz2 is the operator interface of the Operator PC. It starts with rviz/moveit.rviz from smartmanipulator_x_moveit_config and talks to move_group through the MoveIt MotionPlanning plugin. Every plan is computed on the Operator PC; only the execution goes to the Robot PC.

This page walks through a complete session: start, a named goal, planning, execution, a goal set with the interactive marker, the joint view, the gripper and the planner settings. The screenshots were taken with the Robot PC running mock hardware on smx_net; with mock hardware every commanded position becomes the joint state at once, so the arm in RViz2 follows the trajectory exactly.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Check How The Robot PC runs In the Robot PC repository: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up robot_pc The Operator PC runs In this repository: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up operator_pc (Getting started) move_group is ready Its log ends with You can start planning now!

Two ERROR lines in the log at start-up are normal and can be ignored:

Message Meaning No 3D sensor plugin(s) defined for octomap updates No depth camera is configured; the planning scene has no octomap Action server: /recognize_objects not available The Detect button of the Scene Objects tab has no object recognition behind it

docs.title: 1. The window
docs.text:
RViz2 after start: the MotionPlanning panel on the left with the Planning tab, the Displays list below it, and the 3D view on the right with the arm in its current state and the interactive marker at the gripper Area Content Toolbar Interact (move the marker, the default tool), Move Camera, Select MotionPlanning panel Tabs Context, Planning, Joints, Scene Objects, Stored Scenes, Stored States, Status, Manipulation (behind the arrow) Displays Grid, RobotModel (Robot PC state), MotionPlanning, TF — tick a box to show a display 3D view The arm, the goal and the planned path in the fixed frame world

What the 3D view shows:

You see It is Arm in its own colours (light grey, metal parts) The current state, as reported by the Robot PC in /joint_states Orange, semi-transparent arm The goal state (35 % opacity). Where it overlaps the current state the arm looks tan, as right after start Red, green and blue arrows and rings at the gripper The interactive marker on tool_link, the tip of the arm chain Grey arm moving from start to goal The planned path preview after Plan Display Default Shows Grid on 10 cm cells, 2 m × 2 m, in the fixed frame world MotionPlanning on Current state, goal state, interactive marker, planned path RobotModel (Robot PC state) off The model from /robot_description, posed by the Robot PC's /tf TF off All frames of the robot

Camera: left mouse button drag rotates the view around the focal point, middle button (or Shift + left) pans, the wheel zooms. With the Interact tool, a drag that starts on the marker moves the marker; a drag that starts anywhere else rotates the camera.

docs.title: 2. Choose a named goal
docs.text:
In the Planning tab, check Planning Group arm and Start State <current>, then open Goal State. The list has the special entries and the named poses from the SRDF:

The Goal State list of the arm group: <random valid>, <random>, <current>, <same as start>, <previous>, then the named poses home, ready and cad_pose Entry Goal <random valid> A random collision-free state — useful to exercise the planner <random> A random state, may be in collision <current> The present state of the arm (no motion) <same as start> The start state <previous> The goal before the last change home All arm joints at 0 ready j2 0.5, j3 0.8, j5 0.6 rad, others 0 cad_pose j2 0.7416, j3 0.4674, j4 0.1426, j5 0.9151 rad — the pose of the BCN3D CAD assembly

Choose ready. The orange goal arm moves to the pose, the current arm stays where it is, and the marker jumps to the goal's tool_link:

Goal State ready selected: the orange goal arm bends forward, the grey current arm still stands upright

docs.title: 3. Plan and check the preview
docs.text:
Click Plan. move_group plans with OMPL; the time appears under the buttons (here Time: 0.023 s) and Execute becomes active. The grey arm plays the trajectory from the current state to the goal, so you can check the path before anything moves:

After Plan: Time 0.023 under the buttons, Execute enabled, the grey preview arm moving from the upright start towards the orange goal

If the result is not what you want, change the goal and click Plan again; nothing has been sent to the Robot PC yet.

docs.title: 4. Execute
docs.text:
Click Execute. The trajectory goes as a FollowJointTrajectory goal to the Robot PC; the status under the buttons changes to Executed when the controller reports success, and the current arm stands in the goal pose:

After Execute: status Executed, the arm in the ready pose, current and goal state overlap

The two logs show the same execution from both sides:

Operator PC (move_group)
  sending trajectory to arm_controller
  arm_controller started execution
  Goal request accepted!
  Controller 'arm_controller' successfully finished
  Completed trajectory execution with status SUCCEEDED ...

Robot PC (ros2_control_node)
  [arm_controller]: Received new action goal
  [arm_controller]: Accepted new action goal
  [arm_controller]: Goal reached, success!

Plan & Execute does steps 3 and 4 in one click, without the chance to check the preview. Stop cancels a running execution.

docs.title: 5. Set a goal with the interactive marker
docs.text:
The marker sits on tool_link of the goal state. With the Interact tool:

Handle Moves the goal Arrow (red, green, blue) Along that axis of the marker Ring Rotation about that axis Sphere in the centre Freely in the view plane

Grab a handle and drag. While pick_ik finds a solution, the orange goal arm follows the marker:

The marker dragged along its red arrow: the orange goal arm reaches further forward than the grey current arm

Then Plan (and check the preview) and Execute, or Plan & Execute.

Position goals only

The Moveo has five arm joints, so it cannot reach an arbitrary position and orientation. The IK solver matches the tool position and ignores its orientation (rotation_scale: 0.0 in config/kinematics.yaml), so the marker always solves for reachable positions; turning the rings has little or no effect on the goal. See MoveIt 2 configuration for a best-effort orientation.

If the marker is dragged out of reach, the goal arm stops following (no IK solution); drag it back towards the base.

docs.title: 6. Joints tab
docs.text:
The Joints tab lists the joints of the planning group with their values in degrees. Drag a bar to change one joint directly — useful for small corrections, for example of j4_forearm_roll, which the position-only marker does not set:

The Joints tab: j1_base -2°, j2_shoulder 49°, j3_elbow 8°, j4_forearm_roll 24°, j5_wrist 17°, with the Nullspace exploration slider below

The tab header names the state the bars belong to. Nullspace exploration moves the arm inside the set of joint values that keep the tool where it is.

docs.title: 7. The gripper
docs.text:
In the Planning tab, set Planning Group to gripper. The marker disappears: the gripper is a single joint, not a chain. Goal State lists open (gripper 0.0 rad) and closed (gripper 1.4 rad; limit 1.45):

Planning Group gripper and its Goal State list with the named poses open and closed

Choose closed and click Plan & Execute. MoveIt sends a one-joint trajectory to gripper_controller on the Robot PC; the gears, pivot arms and fingers mimic the gripper joint and move with it:

The gripper before (open, left) and after (closed, right) the execution

Switch back to Planning Group arm for arm motions.

docs.title: 8. Speed of the motion
docs.text:
The Velocity Scaling and Accel. Scaling fields in the Planning tab scale the joint limits for each request (0–1). RViz2 starts with 0.10: the arm moves at 10 % of the limits of the robot description (1.0 rad/s for every joint) and of config/joint_limits.yaml (1.0 rad/s²).

Motion (measured with mock hardware, scaling 0.10) Duration Arm home → ready about 9 s Gripper open → closed (1.4 rad) about 15 s

Raise the scaling for faster motions in simulation. The default_*_scaling_factor of 0.3 in joint_limits.yaml applies to requests that do not set a scaling, for example from scripts; RViz2 always sends its own value.

Placeholder limits

The joint limits are placeholders until the Moveo axes are measured on the real arm. With mock hardware every speed works; keep the scaling low when the Robot PC drives real motors.

docs.title: 9. Planner options
docs.text:
Planning tab, Options:

Option Default Meaning Planning Time (s) 5.0 Time limit per planning attempt Planning Attempts 10 Attempts; the best result is kept Velocity / Accel. Scaling 0.10 See above Use Cartesian Path off Straight line of the tool instead of a joint-space path; it needs an IK solution along the whole line, which the 5-DOF arm may not have — leave off unless you need a straight line Collision-aware IK off IK rejects solutions in collision while you drag the marker Approx IK Solutions off Accept approximate IK solutions for the marker Replanning off Plan again if the scene changes during execution

Context tab: the planning pipeline is ompl, the only one configured; the planner <unspecified> uses the pipeline's default planner. Warehouse (a database of stored scenes and states) is not set up and is not needed. Workspace limits the planning volume to a 2 m cube around the origin:

The Context tab: planning library OMPL, pipeline ompl, planner unspecified, warehouse host and port, workspace centre 0 0 0 and size 2 2 2

docs.title: What happens on Execute
docs.text:
1. RViz2 asks move_group to execute the plan.
  2. MoveItSimpleControllerManager sends it as a FollowJointTrajectory goal to arm_controller/follow_joint_trajectory (or gripper_controller/follow_joint_trajectory) on the Robot PC.
  3. The Robot PC's joint_trajectory_controller interpolates it at 100 Hz and commands the hardware (mock now).
  4. joint_state_broadcaster publishes /joint_states; move_group updates the current state and RViz2 redraws the arm.

MoveIt accepts the execution only if the arm starts within 0.02 rad of the plan's start (allowed_start_tolerance), and it aborts it if it takes longer than 1.5 × the planned duration + 1 s. Both settings are in config/moveit_controllers.yaml (MoveIt 2 configuration). If an execution fails, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Saving the layout
docs.text: Panel sizes, the camera and display settings can be saved with File → Save Config. The file in the container is part of the image, so a saved change is lost when the container is recreated; to keep it, copy the changes into ros2_ws/src/smartmanipulator_x_moveit_config/rviz/moveit.rviz and rebuild.

docs.title: move_group without RViz2
docs.text:
To start only move_group (for example to plan from a script or from a second RViz2):

docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml run --rm operator_pc \
    ros2 launch smartmanipulator_x_moveit_config operator.launch.py rviz:=false

Stop the operator_pc service first: both use the fixed address 10.77.0.20. The rviz launch argument (default true) is the only argument of operator.launch.py.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Most problems fall into four groups: the containers cannot start, the GUI does not show, the two computers do not see each other, or MoveIt plans but the Robot PC does not execute. Start every diagnosis with a shell on the network:

docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml run --rm shell

docs.title: Normal messages
docs.text:
Two ERROR lines appear at every start and are harmless:

Message Meaning No 3D sensor plugin(s) defined for octomap updates (move_group) No depth camera is configured Action server: /recognize_objects not available (rviz2) No object recognition behind the Detect button of the Scene Objects tab

docs.title: Start and build
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix network smx_net declared as external, but could not be found The Robot PC is not running, so smx_net does not exist Start the Robot PC first (up robot_pc in its repository) additional_contexts is rejected, or unknown flag: --build-context Docker Compose older than v2.17, or BuildKit disabled Update Docker Desktop / the Compose plugin; do not set DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0 failed to compute cache key: "/ros2_ws/src/smartmanipulator_x/smartmanipulator_x_description": not found The Robot PC repository is not at ../SmartManipulator-X-Robot-PC Clone it side by side, or set SMX_ROBOT_PC_REPO in docker/.env Address already in use for 10.77.0.20 A second operator_pc container (for example from run) holds the fixed address docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml down, then start once /entrypoint.sh: no such file or directory The script was checked out with CRLF line endings The Dockerfile strips CR already; re-clone with .gitattributes in effect (LF) and rebuild

docs.title: Display
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix could not connect to display :0 / qt.qpa.xcb: could not connect The X11 socket is not mounted, or the wrong DISPLAY Windows: Docker Desktop with WSL 2 backend and WSLg (Windows 11). Linux: set the X11 values in docker/.env and run xhost +local:docker Authorization required, but no authorization protocol specified The X server refuses the container Linux: xhost +local:docker in the desktop session Window opens, but the 3D view is black or RViz2 crashes on start OpenGL driver problem Keep SMX_LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 (default); test with glxgears in the shell service RViz2 is slow Software rendering on few cores Expected with llvmpipe; set up a GPU path and SMX_LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=0, or close other displays

docs.title: Discovery and data
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix ros2 node list shows only the local nodes Different ROS_DOMAIN_ID, or not on the same network Same domain on both sides (default 42); both containers on smx_net (docker network inspect smx_net) Nodes are listed, but ros2 topic echo /joint_states stays silent Fast DDS chose shared memory between containers Check FASTDDS_DEFAULT_PROFILES_FILE=/etc/smx/fastdds_udp.xml on both sides; rebuild the image if the file is missing Native Windows ROS 2 does not see the containers Docker Desktop does not route multicast between Windows and container networks Use the shell service instead Discovery works on one computer, not on two Firewall or different subnets Allow UDP between the hosts, same subnet, see Network and DDS

docs.title: Planning and execution
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix move_group waits with Didn't receive robot state (joint angles) with recent timestamp No /joint_states from the Robot PC Check the Robot PC is running and the discovery checks above The robot in RViz2 does not move after Execute The Robot PC did not accept the goal Look at the Robot PC log; ros2 control list_controllers must show arm_controller active Unable to identify any set of controllers that can actuate the specified joints Controller names or joints differ between moveit_controllers.yaml and the Robot PC's controllers.yaml Make them identical; rebuild Action client not connected to action server: arm_controller/follow_joint_trajectory The controller is not running, or DDS does not deliver actions ros2 action list in the shell; restart the Robot PC Execution aborted: start state deviates The arm is more than 0.02 rad away from the plan's start Plan again from the current state (Start State <current>) Execution aborted after a time The trajectory took longer than 1.5 × planned + 1 s Lower the speed scaling, or check the Robot PC controller (100 Hz) is not overloaded The marker does not follow, goal turns red No IK solution: the position is out of reach, or the goal is in collision Move the marker closer to the base; check joint limits Rotating the marker does nothing Expected: the IK ignores orientation (rotation_scale: 0.0) See kinematics Planning failed for reachable goals OMPL found no path in the planning time, or the start state is in collision Planning Time up in the Context tab; Start State <current>; check the collision matrix

docs.title: Model mismatch
docs.text:
If the arm in RViz2 and the Robot PC disagree (different joints, a missing link, errors about unknown joints), the two images were built from different versions of the robot description. Rebuild both from the same Robot PC commit:

# in the Robot PC repository
docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up --build robot_pc
# in this repository
docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up --build operator_pc
